title: Only Joseph receives revelations that command the church
setting: This revelation came at Fayette, New York, in September 1830, shortly before the conference of 26 September. Joseph and Emma Smith had just moved there from Harmony, Pennsylvania. Hiram Page claimed to receive revelations through a stone about Zion and church order. Many members, including Oliver Cowdery and the Whitmer family, accepted them. Earlier that summer Oliver had written commanding Joseph to erase words from the church’s Articles and Covenants. Joseph sought guidance and dictated this revelation for Oliver.
summary: The revelation tells Oliver Cowdery the church will hear him when he teaches by the Comforter. It then says only Joseph Smith is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church, “even as Moses”. Oliver is to be like Aaron, declaring what Joseph receives. He may speak by the Spirit, but he must not write by way of commandment or command Joseph. Oliver is sent to preach to the Lamanites and establish the church among them. The city of Zion’s location is not yet revealed, but it will be “on the borders by the Lamanites”. Oliver is to tell Hiram Page privately that his stone writings come from Satan. All things are to be done in order and by common consent.

contextNote.title: One channel for the church’s commandments
contextNote.text: Hiram Page’s stone writings had won followers, and Oliver himself had tried to command Joseph. Verse 2 answers both problems at once. Only Joseph is appointed to receive commandments and revelations for the church. Verse 7 gives the reason: Joseph holds “the keys of the mysteries”. Verse 4 still lets Oliver speak and teach as the Comforter leads. Verse 5 limits his writing, which must be “by wisdom,” not by commandment. Verse 13 adds that all things must be done in order and by common consent. In this passage “appointed” means the one person authorized to give binding direction to the whole church.

ldsText: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “All Things Must Be Done in Order” draws its title from verse 13 of this revelation. How do verses 2 and 13 work together to protect a church from confusion like that caused by Hiram Page’s stone?
reviewNote: Read all 16 verses. Official heading gives Fayette, September 1830, to Oliver Cowdery, about Hiram Page’s stone, before the conference. JSP historical introduction read for Oliver’s earlier letter on the Articles and Covenants, the move from Harmony in early September, and the 26 September conference. Revelation Book 1 copy is misdated 1831 by scribal error. indian-lands stands for “the borders by the Lamanites” (v. 9) and the mission destination. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote misread verses 4–5: verse 4 allows Oliver to speak even by way of commandment; verse 5 restricts only his writing. Also removed the claim that verse 13 says the order is "confirmed" by common consent.
